s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Developed rhinorrhea and recovered from COVID-19
Worsening right-sided headache started 1 week after COVID-19 recovery
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Developed rhinorrhea and recovered from COVID-19
Worsening right-sided headache started 1 week after COVID-19 recovery
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells

shortlist.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and extension of inflammation into the apex

shortlist.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rhinorrhea and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement

shortlist.label: Acute Bacterial Sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus and worsening right-sided headache

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of vision loss, severe pain on ocular motion, and limited visual acuity are consistent with Orbital Apex Syndrome, which is also supported by the imaging findings of bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and extension of inflammation into the apex.

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: While the patient has an elevated Serum IgG4 level and histopathologic findings of IgG4-positive plasma cells, the acute presentation and severity of symptoms are more consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process like Orbital Apex Syndrome.

rejected.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of fungal elements in the pathology or imaging findings, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: Similar to Invasive Aspergillosis, there is no evidence of fungal infection, and the patient's symptoms and findings are more consistent with a bacterial or inflammatory process.

rejected.label: Acute Bacterial Sinusitis
rejected.why: While the patient has positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus, the severity of symptoms and involvement of the orbital apex are more consistent with Orbital Apex Syndrome, which can be a complication of sinusitis.

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease is not the best fit due to the acute presentation
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms developed rapidly, which is not typical for IgG4-related disease, which usually has a more chronic course.
